featured_reviews.name: Anna Sharafulina
featured_reviews.review_text:
First, they’ll bombard you with enrollment messages for weeks.

Then, they’ll give you the class timing a week in advance.

After that, they’ll confirm the location the evening before the class.

Then they’ll conveniently forget to inform you that the class has been rescheduled.

You’ll arrive on time, only to find a locked door, after planning your entire day around the class.

I can understand human factor of the receptionist. But then why play a show, like you are calling a teacher to know where he/she is and then say “actually you know what happened, the class was rescheduled” like I supposed to know about it. And I actually supposed to. From you. In advance.

The worst thing a school can do is relentlessly chase prospective students for enrollment and payment, only to completely disregard their time, effort, and money once they’ve signed up.

I rearranged my schedule, canceled other commitments, paid for transportation, and showed up at the exact time I was instructed to be there. Only after I arrived and multiple calls from my side was I told that the class timing had changed and that nobody had informed me.

Mistakes happen, but basic communication and respect for students’ time should be the minimum standard for any educational institution. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.
P.s. the school situated in a slum looking area in a quite dirty building, so vibe is not vibing. Can’t say anything about the teachers though, maybe they are nice.
Thank you.

featured_reviews.name: Suraj Landge
featured_reviews.review_text:
I enrolled myself in NMIMS School Of Performing Arts in 2018. Although I had no prior professional music training and was mostly self taught, I was able to crack the audition and the interview. Within next six months I was able to play and sing several different genres. I was comfortable with complex time signatures and my music theory and basics were strong. NMIMS SOPA not only focuses on the performing aspect but also pushes their students to analyse, compose, arrange and produce music.

The campus is small. But, each and every single practice rooms are sound proof with good acoustics, amazing high end instruments ( 2 Steinway Grand pianos, few upright pianos, around 15 digital pianos, teles, strats, PRS guitars, Marshall tube Amps, Fender reverb amps, Nord keyboards, over 10 drum kits to name a few. )

Most of all, the faculty members are internationally known for their playing. We’ve also had many master classes from Artists like Sanjay Divecha, Trilok Gurtu, Guthrie Govan and Marcus Gilmore.

For those who are still unsure due to some scuffle between the NMIMS management , I’d suggest them to directly contact the dean or schedule an appointment to clear any confusion. Every college has its own ups and downs, it’s about how much you learn from it.

I’ve enjoyed every moment of learning from this college :)
